title: Two locally finite type field structures on an algebraic space give algebraically dependent scalars
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $E/S$ be an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $k_1,k_2$ be fields [def-weil-field] with maps $\operatorname{Spec}k_i\to S$, and let $p_i:E\to\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ be $S$-morphisms. Assume each $p_i$ is locally of finite type: for every representable etale scheme chart $U\to E$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], the scheme map $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $F$ be a field and $e:\operatorname{Spec}F\to E$ an $S$-morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Write $j_i:k_i\hookrightarrow F$ for the field homomorphism induced by $p_i e$. Then for every $\lambda\in k_1$, the element $j_1(\lambda)$ is algebraic over $j_2(k_2)$: it is a root of a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in $j_2(k_2)$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The assertion also holds with $1$ and $2$ interchanged. No reducedness, connectedness, quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis on $E\to S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), applied on the reduced closure of a point in an etale scheme chart, then mapped into a common extension of the point field. This is the scalar consequence of the integral-closure equality, allowing arbitrary algebraic spaces via their defining etale charts.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $q:U\to E$. By the scheme-test definition, $V=U\times_E\operatorname{Spec}F$ is a scheme and $V\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is surjective, so choose $v\in V$. The canonical residue-field morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to V$, $L=\kappa(v)$, gives a field embedding $h:F\hookrightarrow L$ and a map $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$ with $qu=e\operatorname{Spec}h$. In particular the two scalar maps to $L$ obtained through $U$ are exactly $h j_i$.

source.place: Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space), atlas and scheme-test surjectivity; schemes.tex Tag 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points), preceding discussion of residue-field morphisms

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U_0\subseteq U$ containing the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Write $U_0\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$. The map $u$ factors through $U_0$ and therefore gives a ring map $\psi:A\to L$. By hypothesis $p_iq:U\to\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ is locally of finite type. Applying the all-affine-pairs criterion to $U_0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ shows that $A$ is finitely generated as a $k_i$-algebra for each $i$. Write $\alpha_i:k_i\to A$ for these scalar maps; functoriality gives $\psi\alpha_i=h j_i$.

Set $\mathfrak p=\ker\psi$ and $B=A/\mathfrak p$. Since $L$ is a field, $1\notin\mathfrak p$ and $ab\in\mathfrak p$ implies $a\in\mathfrak p$ or $b\in\mathfrak p$; hence $B$ is a nonzero domain. The induced map $\bar\psi:B\hookrightarrow L$ is injective. If $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ generate $A$ over $k_i$, their images generate $B$ over $k_i$. Thus $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ has both structure maps locally of finite type, by the affine-cover definition. Write $\rho_i:k_i\hookrightarrow B$ for the scalar maps; they are injective because their composites with $\bar\psi$ are the embeddings $h j_i$.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), affine prime-quotient reduction supplied here; elementary quotient-generator argument

proof.text: The domain $B$ is reduced: if $b^n=0$ with $n>0$, repeated cancellation in a domain gives $b=0$. The affine reducedness criterion makes $Z$ reduced. Its zero ideal is prime, and $V((0))=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is irreducible by the prime-spectrum criterion; it contains the zero prime, so it is nonempty. Irreducibility implies connectedness. Consequently $Z$ satisfies all the topological and reducedness hypotheses needed for scalar-field uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 01J2 (lemma-affine-reduced); algebra.tex Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible), (2); topology.tex immediately after Tag 004V (definition-irreducible-components)

proof.text: Apply scalar-field uniqueness to the nonempty connected reduced scheme $Z$ and its two locally finite type field structures. Its global-section ring is $B$. Let $C_i\subset B$ be the subring of elements satisfying a monic polynomial over $\rho_i(k_i)$; the cited theorem gives $C_1=C_2$. For $\lambda\in k_1$, $\rho_1(\lambda)$ belongs to $C_1$ by the polynomial $T-\rho_1(\lambda)$. Hence it belongs to $C_2$: there are $n\ge1$ and $c_0,\ldots,c_{n-1}\in k_2$ such that $\rho_1(\lambda)^n+\sum_{r<n}\rho_2(c_r)\rho_1(\lambda)^r=0$ in $B$. Degree zero cannot occur because a monic constant polynomial is $1$ and $B$ is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), equality of integral closures, specialized to the affine domain B

proof.text: Apply $\bar\psi$ to the equation. Using $\bar\psi\rho_i=h j_i$, it becomes $h(j_1(\lambda)^n+\sum_{r<n}j_2(c_r)j_1(\lambda)^r)=0$. The field homomorphism $h$ is injective, so the expression inside $h$ is zero in $F$. Thus $T^n+\sum_{r<n}j_2(c_r)T^r\in j_2(k_2)[T]$ annihilates $j_1(\lambda)$. It is nonzero because its leading coefficient is $1$. Interchanging the two indices in the same argument proves the other assertion. The construction used only one point of an atlas and one affine neighbourhood, so imposes none of the additional global hypotheses excluded in the statement.
